narration: Your 401k default fund looks fine from the outside. But for 72% of workers who never change it, it quietly destroys $127,000 in retirement money.
visual: Person silhouette sitting at a desk, looking at a glowing tablet showing '401k | DEFAULT FUND | Target Date 2055 | Expense: 0.80%'. Dollar signs float up and drift off the right side of the screen. Dark background, amber dollar signs.

narration: Your target date fund charges 0.8% a year — sounds tiny, right? On a hundred thousand dollars, that's $800 silently drained every year, compounding forever.
visual: A fund statement card springs up from below. It shows 'EXPENSE RATIO: 0.80%' in amber. A dollar counter animates from $0 to $800 labeled 'drained this year alone'. A magnifying glass SVG zooms in on the fee line. Light background.

narration: Right next to it: an index fund at 0.03%. Same market, nearly identical returns — 27 times cheaper. Your plan defaulted you into the expensive one.
visual: Two bar charts grow upward side by side. A tall amber bar labeled 'TARGET DATE 0.80%' towers over a tiny green bar labeled 'INDEX FUND 0.03%'. '27× CHEAPER' text flashes in the center. Dark background.

narration: On $300,000 over 25 years, that fee gap compounds to $127,000 vanished. Not from bad picks — just from fees. And there's still one more hidden drain.
visual: A line chart shows two diverging growth lines: a green line climbing higher (index fund) and an amber dashed line falling behind (target date). A dollar counter climbs from $0 to $127,000 showing the gap. Year label ticks 0 to 25. Light background.

narration: Target date funds load you with bonds even in your thirties. Bonds grow slower than stocks — that safe move costs another $40,000 in growth. Higher fees and slower returns: a double hit.
visual: A donut pie chart springs in. Green slice labeled 'STOCKS 60%' and a pulsing amber slice labeled 'BONDS 40%'. '$40,000 SLOWER' stat appears below. Dark background.

narration: Log into your 401k and check your fund's expense ratio. If it's above 0.1%, swap it for your plan's cheapest index fund. Ten minutes. A hundred twenty-seven thousand dollars.
visual: Two phone cards side by side: amber-bordered card 'Current Fund 0.80%' with an arrow pointing to a green-bordered card 'Index Fund 0.03%' with an animated checkmark. '$127,000 SAVED' springs up large below. Light background.
